walkthroughs.body_html:
Nature & Variety of Living Organisms — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Nature & Variety of Living Organisms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Nature & Variety of Living Organisms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The seven characteristics of living organisms include all of these except:
options: combustion
respiration
nutrition
excretion

mcqs.q: Bacteria are classified as prokaryotes because their cells:
options: have no membrane-bound nucleus
contain chloroplasts
are eukaryotic
have a large nucleus
secreting enzymes and absorbing digested food
photosynthesis in chloroplasts
swallowing and digesting food internally
absorbing light directly

mcqs.q: Viruses are not considered fully living because they:
options: can only reproduce inside a host cell
are made of many cells
carry out photosynthesis
have a nucleus
Viruses are not classed as fully living because they cannot carry out life processes alone and only reproduce inside host cells.
Viruses are living organisms just like bacteria.
Viruses are a type of large bacterium.
Fungi swallow food and digest it internally like animals.
Bacteria have no DNA at all.
Fungi swallow food and digest it internally like animals.
No - bacteria are prokaryotes; their DNA is a loop free in the cytoplasm, with no membrane-bound nucleus.
Bacteria have a nucleus like animal and plant cells.

mcqs.q: How do fungi obtain their food?
options: Bacteria have no DNA at all.
Fungi swallow food and digest it internally like animals.
Fungi make their own food by photosynthesis like plants.
Fungi feed by saprotrophic nutrition: they secrete enzymes onto food and absorb the digested products.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Virus”?
options: A kingdom of organisms with cells having chitin walls that feed by saprotrophic nutrition, secreting enzymes and absorbing the digested food.
A non-cellular infectious particle made of genetic material in a protein coat that can only reproduce inside a living host cell.
A single-celled organism such as a bacterium whose cell has no membrane-bound nucleus; its DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm.
An organism whose cells contain a membrane-bound nucleus, including animals, plants, fungi and protoctists.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Characteristics of life”?
options: A single-celled organism such as a bacterium whose cell has no membrane-bound nucleus; its DNA is a loop in the cytoplasm.
Living organisms carry out movement, respiration, sensitivity, growth, reproduction, excretion and nutrition, remembered as MRS GREN.
An organism whose cells contain a membrane-bound nucleus, including animals, plants, fungi and protoctists.
A group of mostly single-celled eukaryotes, such as Amoeba and Chlorella, that do not fit the plant, animal or fungal kingdoms.

sequence.def: Broadest rank; three domains, e.g. Eukarya
e.g. Animalia; large grouping within a domain
e.g. Mammalia; subdivision of a phylum
